commit_level.attribution_quality: STRONG commit-level, but all files in commit labeled equally
commit_level.leakage_risk: low — commit features use only pre-commit information
commit_level.practical_usefulness: Limited — identifies which commits are risky but not which files within the commit. Entire commit treated as positive.
commit_level.investigation_budget: Commit-level budget means reviewing ALL files in a commit. For commits touching 30+ files (e.g., jinja2), this is impractical.

file_level.label_method: path intersection with corrective commit (Phase 4.8 FILE_PARTIAL only)
file_level.attribution_quality: WEAK — path intersection only. No content, line, or function-level evidence available without repositories.
file_level.leakage_risk: low — file features use only pre-commit information
file_level.practical_usefulness: High potential but currently limited by WEAK attribution. If repository-level evidence improves attribution, this becomes the most practically useful unit.
file_level.investigation_budget: File-level budget means reviewing specific files. Current 108 attributed files across 38 commits is manageable.

function_level.label_method: requires repository history for AST parsing of diffs
function_level.practical_usefulness: Highest potential practical usefulness — functions are the natural unit of code review. But requires repo access.
function_level.investigation_budget: Function-level budget is the most actionable for developers. Currently unavailable.

hunk_level.label_method: requires repository history for diff extraction
hunk_level.practical_usefulness: Most precise but hardest to act on. Requires repo access.
hunk_level.investigation_budget: Hunk-level budget would be extremely targeted but requires infrastructure not available here.

recommendation: FILE_LEVEL has the strongest methodological foundation among available units. It has low label coverage (108/1055 = 10.2%) and WEAK attribution, but it is the only unit with any file-level evidence at all. Commit-level has strong labels but poor practical usefulness (too many files per commit). Function and hunk levels require repository access.
